entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At Gwalior

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Rajendra Kumar Vani

ON THE 12th OF SEPTEMBER, 2024  CRIMINAL APPEAL No. 8304 of 2024  PAHALWAN SINGH PARIHAR  Versus  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH AND OTHERS  Appearance:
 Shri Shailesh Singh Kaurav - Advocate with Shri Anand   learned counsel for the appellant.
Shri Bhanu Pratap Singh Chauhan - Public Prosecutor fo  respondent/State.
ORDER In compliance of earlier order, confirmation of caste certificate has been received.
As per caste certificate the appellant belongs to SC/ST community.

This is the first criminal appeal filed by the appellant for grant of anticipatory bail under Section 14(A) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act for grant of bail relating to FIR No.152 of 2024 registered at Police Station Jigna, District Datia (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 363, 376, 376-D, 506 of I.P.C.and 3(1)(w)(ii) and 3(2)(va) of SC/ST Act added with Section 25/27 of Arms Act.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.

It is further submitted that as per NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-GWL:15716 2 CRA-8304-2024 prosecution case the incident occurred 1 year and six months ago from the date of lodging FIR dated 30.5.2024 and at that time, missing report was lodged and statement of prosecutrix has been recorded which have been filed on behalf of appellant at page No.24.
As per statement of prosecutrix, none has committed any wrong act with her and she did not want to be medically examined.
This FIR has been lodged as a counter blast of FIR bearing Crime No.138/2024 under Section 307 of I.P.C. etc. by co-accused Bharat Parihar against the brother of the prosecutrix and others.
No external injury has been found in the medical report.
At present prosecutrix is living with co-accused Bharat Parihar.
Out of the wedlock a baby girl was born.
They are also getting benefit under Ladli Laxmi Yogna.

sentences.text: Hindu Marriage Act is also pending between prosecutrix and co- accused Bharat Parihar.

Co-accused Bharat Ahirwar and Bharat Parihar have been given benefit of regular bail vide order dated 27.6.2024 passed in Cr.A. No.7011 of 2024 and act of present appellant is similar to the aforesaid co- accused.

The appellant is permanent resident of District Datia (M.P.)
and he is ready to co-operate with the investigation, therefore, it has been prayed that the appellant may be granted the benefit of anticipatory bail.

Per contra, learned counsel for the State vehemently opposed the bail application and submits that present appellant cannot claim parity with aforesaid co-accused as they have been given benefit of regular bail.
The investigation is going on.
The present appellant is required for custodial interrogation.
FSL report and DNA report are also awaited.

He has criminal history; therefore, it has been prayed that the appellant is not entitled for the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-GWL:15716 3 CRA-8304-2024 benefit of anticipatory bail.
Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the case diary available on record.

Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the parties, facts and circumstances of the case,
coupled with the nature of allegation and gravity of offence and the role played by the appellant, this Court is not inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the present appellant.

Accordingly, this first criminal appeal filed by the appellant under Section 14(A) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act for grant of anticipatory bail is hereby dismissed.
